subtitle: Per-symbol coverage of the C++ <numbers> header. SHIPPED 2026-08-25. All 13 constants, each as a variable template over the floating-point type plus a double shorthand, in the nested namespace re_std::numbers. FLOOR IS C++14, NOT C++11: the interface IS a variable template, and there is no back-port that preserves the spelling -- a struct of static members would be different API. Non-floating-point instantiation is rejected via internal::numbers_check, since the standard leaves the primary template undefined and pi_v<int> must be ill-formed rather than silently 3.
legend_blurb: <numbers> supplies the thirteen mathematical constants as variable templates, so pi_v<float> and pi_v<long double> each carry full precision for their own type.

symbols.name: e_v / e
symbols.notes: Euler's number. Literal written with an L suffix and ~37 significant digits so e_v<long double> is exact -- a double literal converted up would silently carry only double precision.
symbols.failure_reason: Ships at C++14, below the workbook C++98 floor. Floor question, not a coverage gap -- the module is currently gated on C++11 and has no C++98 path yet. That is tracked work, not an unreachable tier -- RE_STD_AGENT_README states re_std compiles on C++98 through C++26, and its known-issues table logs blanket C++11 gating (any.hpp) as planned work. See the OPEN tier-floor item.
